commit.message:
TYP: Improve dtype `__getitem__()` overloads

The `generic.__getitem__()` and `void.__getitem__()` annotations already
contained overloads for tuples of `None` with all possible lengths, but
because Python typing specification does not require type checkers to
expand unbounded tuples then type checking could only be expected to
work with arguments the lengths of which are statically known. The
updated overloads enable type checking with all tuples of `None`,
whether or not their lengths are known statically.

The `generic.__getitem__()` and `void.__getitem__()` annotations already
contained overloads for tuples of `None` with all possible lengths, but

whether or not their lengths are known statically.

commit.message:
PERF: Avoid refilling buffers for operands broadcast over them (#32595)

This optimizes two things: First the buffered iterator now allows buffer re-use reliably, but this  was not enabled in the non-reduce iteration loop (maybe accidentally).
Second, when the copy to the buffer can use trivial copies, this it now uses a direct copy approach for speed.

Especially the buffer-reuse can make a large speed difference when it kicks in.

commit.message:
ENH: Finish the fastcall conversion of the scalar method forwarders (#32585)

moved the 36 scalar method forwarders that take keyword arguments to `METH_FASTCALL`. This finishes the issue:

* The argument-less forwarders (`tolist`, `item`, `swapaxes`, `conj`,
  `conjugate`, `nonzero`, `fill`, `transpose`, `__deepcopy__`) and
  `void.getfield` use `METH_FASTCALL` as well, so `gentype_generic_method`,
  which built an argument tuple per call, could be removed.
* The forwarding calls `PyObject_VectorcallMethod` with an interned name
  instead of `PyObject_GetAttrString`.
* The ndarray methods the scalars forward to are converted where that is
  straightforward: `item`, `tolist`, `nonzero`, `conj`, `conjugate`, `fill`,
  `swapaxes`, `transpose`, `byteswap`, `setfield`, `__copy__`, `__deepcopy__`.
  `item` is the one that tends to be called in a loop.

PERF: use the vectorcall calling convention for ndarray.__array_function__

Four required arguments went through `PyArg_ParseTupleAndKeywords` for a body
that is a few type checks.  Saves ~40-80 ns per call for subclasses forwarding
via `super().__array_function__(...)`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

PERF: use the vectorcall calling convention for ndarray.reshape

Besides the tuple `METH_VARARGS` requires, `reshape` used
`NpyArg_ParseKeywords`, which allocates a second, empty one to parse the two
keyword-only arguments.  Neither is built now unless needed: 1.24x-1.97x.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

PERF: parse scalar constructor arguments without PyArg_ParseTupleAndKeywords

The single argument scalar `tp_new` slots take a positional argument only.
Add a fast path for that and leave the rest, always an error, to the generic
parser, so the error messages are unchanged.

`np.bool_` is 1.30x faster to construct, `np.int64` and `np.float32` 1.13x.

commit.message:
ENH: implement `np.minmax` (#32231)

Implements np.minmax using the new ability to register reduction loops to ufuncs implemented in #31816

The loops are implemented in the existing .c.src files with the np.minimun/maximum loops and using exactly the same optimizations and SIMD as them. Two new files minmax.cpp and minmax.h are created just to create the ufunc and initialize the array methods.
I found this to be by far the easiest setup to do now. The other option would be porting the whole loops_minmax.dispatch.c.src to highway and using only c++ but that is a more complicated change with a way more difficult review so I did not do that.

minmax is not a method on the ndarray like min and max are. The only thing exposed in the top-level API is the new np.minmax function. The minimummaximum ufunc is not exposed as np.minimummaximum like np.minimum and np.maximum are as I do not believe there's much use in that. If we ever need it, it's a very simple change.

We should also consider adding a nanminmax in a follow-up PR for completeness and also adding a masked array aware implementation (either by making minmax a method on the ndarray or only by a np.ma.minmax).

Signed-off-by: Iason Krommydas <iason.krom@gmail.com>
